settings.kicker: A destination for serious GT anglers
settings.heading:
Come for the GTs.
Fish beyond
the ordinary.
settings.text:
Cast big poppers and stickbaits into powerful currents along remote reefs. Socotra is a demanding giant-trevally fishery, with shallow water, rocky structure and fish that test every part of your setup.

Our team has explored these waters for more than a decade. Your guides use their knowledge of the coast, currents and seasonal conditions to shape each fishing day.

settings.text: Giant trevally as the primary target

settings.heading: One island. Many possibilities.
settings.intro: Build your trip around giant trevally, with other fishing options when conditions allow.
settings.strip_text: Spanish mackerel · Yellowfin tuna · Jobfish · Groupers · Coral trout · Emperor

settings.heading: Extreme popping
settings.text: Big poppers, sinking stickbaits and strong tackle. Powerful fish, shallow reefs and hard-running currents make this the signature Socotra experience.

settings.heading: Jigging
settings.text: Work deeper structure for groupers, jobfish, amberjack and trevally. Bring both a lighter and a heavier jigging setup to suit different depths.

settings.heading: Light casting
settings.text: Explore lighter fishing from the boat or shore for bluefin trevally, snapper and other species. Offshore opportunities can include mackerel, dorado and tuna.

settings.heading: Choose your fishing window.
settings.intro: Spring and autumn are the core fishing windows. Your guides plan around the conditions on the water.
settings.note: Strong winds can limit access to exposed spots outside these windows. Exact departures and the daily fishing plan are confirmed by our team.

settings.heading: March — April
settings.text: A key window for fishing Socotra’s GT grounds before the summer winds.

settings.heading: October — November
settings.text: Another core window for GT fishing. October can also bring Spanish mackerel migrations.

settings.heading: Choose your expedition.
settings.note: Trip pricing, confirmed departures and package details are supplied personally. Choose a preferred window in the enquiry form.

settings.heading:
Four anglers.
Two boats.
One shared obsession.
settings.text:
The standard trip fishes from two local fibreglass boats, approximately eight metres long, with international guides accompanying the groups.

Your fishing day follows the conditions: target GTs with heavy casting tackle, work deeper water with jigs, or explore lighter options when the opportunity is right.
settings.image_alt: Local fishing boats beneath the remote cliffs of Socotra
settings.caption: The boats and coastline you’ll fish from.

settings.label: Guiding
settings.value: International guide with each boat group

settings.heading:
Sleep by the sea.
Wake up to fish.
settings.text:
Stay in an individual double-size tent with a mattress, sheets and pillows. Shared dining and kitchen tents bring the group together after fishing.

A camp cook prepares meals from available local ingredients. Fresh-water showers, a generator, an interpreter, a jeep and satellite phones support camp life. Soft drinks are included.

This is a remote fishing camp with simple facilities and limited supplies. Come for the fishing and the island, with an expedition mindset.
settings.image_alt: Sleeping tents at Wildsea’s Socotra fishing camp
settings.caption: A tented camp, not a hotel. The coast is part of the experience.

settings.kicker: From first enquiry to first cast
settings.heading: Plan your trip with our team.

settings.question: How do I get to Socotra?
settings.answer: Our team coordinates the Socotra flight arrangements and helps plan the connections for your departure. The original itinerary refers to routes through Abu Dhabi, Dubai or Cairo; current routes and schedules are confirmed when you book.

settings.question: What about the visa and passport?
settings.answer: We help arrange the Socotra visa using the passport information required for your trip. Ask our team to confirm current entry rules and passport validity requirements.

settings.question: Is this trip right for my fishing experience?
settings.answer: GT popping here is physically demanding and requires strong tackle and confidence handling powerful fish. Tell us about your experience and goals so we can recommend the right trip.

settings.question: What should I know about travel cover and preparation?
settings.answer: Travel, medical and evacuation insurance are required for the expedition. Confirm current travel advice and preparation requirements before travelling.

settings.question: Are catches and fishing spots guaranteed?
settings.answer: No. Fishing depends on wind, sea conditions, currents and fish activity. Our guides adjust the daily plan around the conditions. Gallery photographs show past experiences, not guaranteed results.

settings.question: How are dates and prices confirmed?
settings.answer: Send a booking enquiry with your preferred window. Our team personally confirms departures, space, pricing and terms before anything is booked.
